$comment: Machine-readable component contracts for Wyrd's Evidence Thread design system. Every entry is implemented in src/lib/components and, when `catalog` is true, registered in src/lib/registry.ts (parity enforced by src/lib/registry.test.ts). `catalog: true` marks a component a future composed view may place by name: its props are typed, JSON-safe and semantic. `catalog: false` marks trusted application code — chrome that resolves tenant identity, session state and navigation — which an authored view must never be able to place, replace or impersonate. `consumers` lists the accepted product mock pages that require the component; a shared component earns its place only with at least two. The rendered reference is ./renders/styleguide.html.

altitudes.quiet: workbench default — 1px --border rule, 2px radius, no elevation
altitudes.raised: the page's single attention surface — 1px --text rule, no elevation
altitudes.flat: subordinate block — 1px --border-soft rule, no fill change

ownership.$comment: Evidence Thread semantics. See DESIGN.md 'Never colour alone': status pairs such as --ok and --danger can collapse under colour-vision deficiency, so no meaning in this system may rest on hue alone.
ownership.rule: Indigo (--declare) is Declaration, links, selection, focus, and the primary action. Green (--observe) is observed fact. Lime (--evidence) is reserved for retained Evidence, the Wyrd mark spine, and evidence-capture feedback — never a secondary action, hover, or wash. Lime is a fill carrying --evidence-ink, never text on a light surface.
ownership.redundancy: Status carries a glyph, thresholds carry a tick, chart series carry a dash and a marker. Colour is never the sole carrier of a meaning.

rules: named Panel, never Card: a Wyrd Card is a registered domain record, a panel is only a surface it may be drawn on
1px rule, 2px radius, no decorative elevation
quiet = --border rule; raised = --text rule marking the page's single attention surface; flat = --border-soft rule for a subordinate block
wide spans grid-column 1 / -1
accent = the page's single dominant work region: a --declare-soft head over a --surface body; at most one accent panel per page
container-type: inline-size so contained components respond to the panel, not the viewport
primary = --declare fill with --declare-ink label — the one strong action on a surface
secondary = neutral --surface-2 fill with --text label; lime is reserved for retained Evidence and never marks an action
ghost = surface fill, no accent
href renders an <a> with identical treatment, so a catalog-safe view offers navigation without a callback crossing the contract
1px --border rule, 2px radius, no shadow; hover moves to --surface-hover (or a stronger --declare on primary)
no lift, sink, or offset motion: state is carried by fill and rule, not by displacement
focus-visible draws an explicit 2px --declare outline with offset so it stays visible on every fill
tone is a status signal, not decoration
tone drives border, label, and tint from one --bc custom property; --ok/--warn/--danger each clear 4.5:1 as text on --surface and --bg in both modes
1px border in tone colour, 12% tinted fill, 2px radius

MUST render an aria-hidden glyph before the label — ok=✓ warn=! danger=✕ running=●. Status hues can collapse under colour-vision deficiency, so a colour-only badge makes pass and fail identical for some readers.
neutral takes no glyph and no tint: 'neutral' means no status, and a 12% --muted wash lands at 4.46:1 in dark, which the contrast contract rejects
states one applied filter as key + value, never an unlabeled value
removal is a link to the same route minus that param — never a callback, so filter state stays in the URL and stays restorable
the ✕ carries an aria-label naming the filter it removes
the value ellipsizes; the chip never grows past its container
a native <select>: keyboard operation, screen-reader labeling and the mobile picker come from the platform, not from local menu code
the visible <label> is bound by id — a filter control is never labeled by placement alone
auto submits the enclosing form on change; the component takes no callback, so the destination stays a server-owned action or GET route
time-range control is this component with range options, not a separate component

appearance:none plus a wrapper caret gives the control the workbench geometry — 1px --border rule, 2px radius, --surface-hover on hover, 2px --declare focus ring — while the element underneath stays a real <select>. The option list is still drawn by the OS; that is the trade for free keyboard operation, a real mobile picker and correct screen-reader semantics.

the option list is styled through customizable select (appearance: base-select + ::picker(select)) inside an @supports guard. Where that is unsupported the browser draws its own popup and nothing else changes — the element is always a real <select>, so keyboard operation, the mobile picker and screen-reader semantics never depend on the enhancement.
header is plain surface (not gray) relying on a 1px --border bottom rule
selection wash uses --declare-soft plus a 3px --declare inset left marker, never lime — selection is positional as well as tinted
1px --border-soft row dividers, last row borderless
an irreducibly wide table scrolls rather than dropping columns; the scroller is role=region with an aria-label and tabindex=0 so a keyboard-only reader can focus and pan it

a row is interactive only when it carries a link: tbody tr:has(a) takes a --surface-hover wash and an inset --declare marker on focus-visible, and the linked cell underlines. A static readout row gets no hover, so the treatment never promises a click that is not there.
value is set in --font-sans (Familjen Grotesk 700) with tabular numerals
delta trend up = --ok, down = --danger, and the delta text states the direction so the tone is never the only signal
min-width:0 + overflow:hidden so wide values never blow out a grid track
native <details>/<summary>: open state, keyboard operation and the expanded/collapsed announcement come from the platform
open is the initial state only — the element owns it afterwards
1px --border-soft divider between summary and body, matching the internal-divider rule

props.state: loading | empty | partial | error | unauthorized | absent
props.title: string

rules: the one place the workbench says there is nothing to draw and why — no surface silently renders an empty region
the state word is always written out beside the glyph; the dashed border and tone are secondary
loading takes role=status and aria-busy so the wait is announced; every other state takes role=note
code carries the server's stable Wyrd error code verbatim and never a stack, connection detail or invented UI vocabulary
absent is the earned-absent inset: an optional section the server has nothing for, stated rather than hidden
--code-bg block with --code-text in --font-mono (Fragment Mono), 2px radius, horizontally scrollable, dark in both modes
optional copy button via navigator.clipboard; copied feedback is a written word plus glyph, and may take the --evidence fill because it confirms capture
renders text, never markup: the code prop is escaped content, not HTML

props.title: string
props.state: ok | loading | empty | partial | unauthorized | error

rules: the one frame every Wyrd chart is drawn in: measure, unit, latest value, freshness, visible range, source, canonical link and the unavailable states
a non-ok state renders a StateBlock in place of the plot and NEVER a latest value — a stale, absent or unauthorized reading shown as a number is a health claim the server never made
partial draws the plot and the partial notice together; it never silently presents an incomplete series as complete
freshness and range use <time datetime> so the instant is machine-readable, not just formatted prose
composes Panel and StateBlock; it is a frame, never one component per metric and never a universal chart
inline SVG 300x148, multi-series, dashed gridlines

series take no colour prop: stroke, stroke-dasharray and marker shape are chosen by series position from a fixed four-style table; more than four series are rejected, so a serialized view can never name a token

each series MUST carry a distinct dash and marker (solid square, '6 3' circle, '2 3' triangle, '8 2 2 2' diamond) in --declare, --observe, --text, --muted, and the legend MUST mirror both as a line sample, not a block swatch. Hue alone cannot separate two percentiles.
a threshold is drawn as a labeled dashed rule plus a positional tick on the axis — never an unlabeled red line

values are reported by a tooltip pinned to the point under the cursor. It is not pointer-only: focusing the plot opens it on the most recent point and arrow/Home/End walk it, so a keyboard or touch reader reaches every value. It anchors inward at the ends of the range and never takes pointer events.
inline SVG 300x148, --declare fill, value above and category under every bar
bars take no colour prop; the reading is positional and textual, and the SVG carries an aria-label naming every category and value
90x24 polyline, no fill; shape carries the trend
neutral geometry only: shape carries the trend beside a labeled value, never status or health
212px sidebar + topbar + main grid; 1px --border rules between regions on a neutral --bg canvas
trusted application chrome — not catalog: it frames every authored view and must never be placeable by one
nav groups; active item takes a --declare-soft wash, --declare label, and a 3px --declare inset marker — positional as well as tinted
brand slot is the Wyrd mark (logo.svg / logo-light.svg, generated from palette.json) followed by the 'Wyrd' wordmark in --font-sans
carries the five product entries and no per-item kind bar: navigation is not a typed plane
trusted application chrome — not catalog: it owns navigation, which an authored view must never redirect
breadcrumb + search + environment badge
the environment reads through Badge so its state carries a glyph and text; a bare coloured dot would make the state hue-only
hosts the ProductPill immediately after the wordmark
trusted application chrome — not catalog: it carries tenant identity and the principal menu
applies data-mode and the shared font shorthands; every token in this file resolves beneath it
trusted application chrome — not catalog: it is composed by the layout, never placed by name
uppercase --font-mono, 10px, 700, .08em tracking
wyrd = --declare fill + --declare-ink
--declare-ink on --declare holds ≥4.5:1 in both modes (asserted by gen-theme.mjs)
1px border, 2px radius — sits immediately after the Wyrd wordmark in the Topbar
names the product layer the current surface belongs to; it is identity, never a control
trusted application chrome — not catalog: an authored view must never label itself as a product layer
